title: 帖撒羅尼迦前書

content: 帖撒羅尼迦前書  1:1-10莊劉真光師母 5/7/2000前 言帖撒羅尼迦教會位於希臘半島的馬其頓，是保羅第二次旅行佈道時所建立的。當他寫帖撒羅尼迦前書時，這個教會才成立很短的時間。I. 問安(1:1)1. 恩惠2. 平安II. 感謝(1:2-10)這段文字在希臘原文只是一個句子。在此保羅為帖撒羅尼迦教會感謝神：1. 為他們美好的基督徒生活見證A. 因信心所作的工夫B. 因愛心所受的勞苦C. 因盼望我們主耶穌基督所存的忍耐2. 為他們是蒙神所揀選的保羅確知他們是蒙揀選的原因：A. 保羅把福音傳給他們的工作(1) 言語(2) 權能(3) 聖靈(4) 充分的確信B. 他們效法了保羅，也效法了主(1) 在大患難中蒙聖靈所賜的喜樂，並領受真道。(2) 他們作了馬其頓和亞該亞所有信徒的榜樣(3) 作榜樣的連鎖反應：主 →保羅 →帖撒羅尼迦教會 →馬其頓和亞該亞所有的信徒C. 主的道從他們那裏傳出去(1) 馬其頓、亞該亞和各處(2) 各處的人都在傳述帖撒羅尼迦信徒的見證a. 離棄偶像歸向神b. 服事又真又活的神c. 等候祂兒子從天降臨討論問題：(1) 請分享教會在「信心」、「愛心」、「盼望」三方面有那些可以向神獻上感謝的，並在分享之後，齊心向神獻上感謝的禱告。(2) 請討論「作榜樣」的重要性，並分享我們個人或教會是否成為其他信徒或其他教會的榜樣？(3) 請討論「耶穌的再來」對我們現在的生活，有甚麼實際的影響？傳道者的典範帖撒羅尼迦前書 2:1-16莊劉真光師母 5/21/2000前 言2:1-16乃是1:5-10的延伸。2:1-12與1:5,9兩節相對照，但顯然這是保羅從提摩太的報告中，知悉仇敵對他的批評與指控後(3:5-6)，所提出的駁斥與辯護。2:13-16則與1:6-8, 9b-10相對照，保羅再次為帖撒羅尼迦教會對福音的接受而感謝神，但其目的是進一步地辯白。I. 教牧的典範(2:1-12)1. 傳道的能力(2:1-2)A. 工作的果效B. 放膽傳福音2. 傳道的動機與行為(2:3-8)A. 無不良動機與行為1) 勸勉不是出於錯誤、污穢或詭詐2) 不是要討人喜歡3) 沒有用諂媚的話4) 沒有藏著貪心5) 沒有向人求榮耀B. 存高尚動機與行為1) 被神驗中，受託傳福音，單討察驗人心之神的喜悅。2) 存心溫柔，如同母親3. 傳道者生活的榜樣(2:9-10)A. 日夜殷勤作工B. 聖潔、公義、無可指摘4. 傳道的工作態度與目的(2:11-12)A. 勸勉、安慰、囑咐，如同父親B. 目的II. 再次感謝神(2:13-16)1. 為此2. 感謝神的原因A. 帖撒羅尼迦教會對福音的接受1) 認為是神的道而領受了2) 神的道運行在他們心中B. 帖撒羅尼迦教會忍受逼迫1) 效法在猶太基督的教會2) 猶太人的罪討論問題：(1)在你屬靈成長的過程中，曾否有屬靈的父親或母親，成為你的榜樣和引導？請分享。(2)如果我們在教會中，聽見對傳道人的批評論斷，我們應當如何行？(3)你曾否在為主傳福音，或在生活上，因遵行神的旨意而受逼迫？請分享。牧者的心腸帖撒羅尼迦前書 2:17-3:13莊劉真光師母 5/28/2000前 言保羅在2:1-16，針對仇敵對他的詆毀提出駁斥與辯護之後，在2:17-3:13他進一步地向帖撒羅尼迦教會表明他身為牧者的心腸。然而這也是繼續他的辯白。I. 牧者深切的愛(2:17-3:5)1. 保羅切望到他們那裏去A. 熱切的愛B. 撒旦的阻擋C. 切望去他們那裏的原因2. 差提摩太去他們那裏A. 保羅的愛與犧牲B. 目的C. 信徒必受逼迫II. 牧者的安慰(3:6-10)1. 得安慰的原因A. 他們保守信心和愛心B. 他們對保羅的想念2. 得安慰、受激勵3. 感謝與禱告A. 感謝B. 禱告III. 牧者的禱告(3:11-13)1. 禱告的對象2. 禱告的內容A. 祈求的項目B. 祈求的目的討論問題：(1) 你曾否帶領人信主？曾否遭遇挫折？是否仍然堅持？如何克服困難？請討論分享。(2) 你曾否因別人(特別是你所帶領的人)的信心與愛心而受激勵？請分享。(3) 你平時的禱告內容為何？曾否為別人代禱？請討論分享。牧者的勸勉帖撒羅尼迦前書 4:1-12莊祖鯤牧師 6/4/2000前 言(4:1-2)保羅在帖撒羅尼迦前書的前三章是比較私人性質的，一方面為自己辯護，同時也向信徒表明他的愛心與關切。最後兩章，則是警告與勸勉，也就是教導信徒有關真理的實踐部份。I. 過聖潔的生活(4:3-8)第一世紀的羅馬帝國，尤其是希臘地區的生活特色，就是性的放縱。因此保羅要提醒在帖撒羅尼迦的信徒，如何在這樣一個罪惡的環境中，潔身自愛。1. 遠避淫行─消極方面A. 不放縱邪情私欲B. 不要「越份」2. 成為聖潔─積極方面A. 持守「聖潔」與尊貴B. 保守「身體」的純潔─ 「身體」原文是「器皿」，少數譯本將之譯為「妻子」(RSV)，但是多數譯本譯成「身體」。II. 以愛心彼此相待(4:9-12)1. 要更加努力(4:9-10)─ 「弟兄相愛」(Philadelphia)在希臘文中，通常只用在親兄弟之間，但是在聖經中卻常用在信徒之間。因為教會是「神的家」，因此信徒之間的關係，往往比親兄弟姊妹還親。2. 要殷勤作工、自食其力(4:11-12)─ 「立志作安靜人」或可譯為「立志過淡泊的生活」，也就是「不攪擾別人，不成為別人的累贅」之意。─ 希臘人鄙視體力勞動，視為奴隸的工作。因此希臘人常常遊手好閑，不務正業。但是聖經卻堅持勞力是高貴的，每個人都該親手做工(帖後3:10-12；弗4:28)。結 論討論問題：(1) 在現今這個邪惡淫亂的時代，傳播媒體、娛樂場所及工作環境中，都充斥著色情的引誘。我們要如何遠避淫行？請討論分享。(2) 在「彼此相愛」的教訓上，我們需要常以為虧欠(羅13:8)。我們團契在那些方面需要加強呢？請提出具體的建議及行動方案。(3) 在教會中，有時我們會遇見一些不肯自食其力的基督徒，他們必須長期依賴別人的幫助。我們應該如何幫助他們？人生的夢魘帖撒羅尼迦前書 4:13-5:11莊祖鯤牧師 6/11/2000前 言在二十世紀末，人們對於「世界末日」有非常不同的反應，有的人焦慮不安，有的人漠不關心。對於死亡，人們也同樣的有見仁見智的看法。基督徒應該如何看「生死」與「世界末日」這兩個問題呢？保羅在本段聖經就是在探討這兩個重要的問題。這兩段經文，都以「論到」為始(4:13; 5:1)，以「彼此勸慰」作結(4:18; 5:11)。I. 對死亡─要存著盼望(4:13-18)1. 關於「基督的再來」(v.14-16)─ 對於已死的親友，我們的傷心是人之常情，因為「天人永隔」畢竟是人之大慟。但是唯有基督徒能有與已死的信徒「再相會」的盼望，這是我們極大的安慰。2. 關於信徒的「復活」(v.14-16)─ 聖經上經常稱已死的信徒「睡了」，而英文的「墳場」(cemetery)也是來自希臘文的「睡覺之處」。但是聖經上從未稱耶穌「睡了」，總是說祂「死了」。因為耶穌基督是為承擔人類的罪，與神隔離了，所以祂「死了」。信徒則因耶穌的代贖，使我們的肉體雖然「睡了」，靈魂卻能與神同在。─ 信徒的復活，將得到一個嶄新的身體，是有榮光的「天上形體」(林前15:35-52)。3. 關於信徒「被提」(v.17a)─ 「被提」一詞的英文(Rapture)來自拉丁文(rapto)，意思是「被抓住」。聖經中只提到信徒被提的事，卻未明確提到被提的時機，因此才有「災前被提」、「災中被提」及「災後被提」的三種理論。4. 關於「與主永遠同在」(v.17b)II. 對主再來─要儆醒謹守(5:1-10)1. 不要掉以輕心(v.1-3)─ 對於主的再臨，有的人焦慮不安，覺得已經迫在眉睫了，甚至於傾家蕩產，以迎接主再來；有的人則漠不關心，認為是天方夜譚。這兩種極端的態度都是不正確的。─ 對於主的再臨，人們最有興趣的題目可能是：『何日君再來？』。但是聖經卻一再地告訴我們，祂再臨的時候日期 是無法預測的(徒1:7)。但是歷代以來，總是有人妖言惑眾，甚至引發動亂。我們要記得主耶穌的警告與提醒。─ 用孕婦生產來預表末日的災難，一方面表示結局是無可避免的，但是另一方面也表示時間卻是無法預知的。2. 要保持儆醒謹守(v.4-8)─ 「光明」與「黑暗」，「白晝」與「黑夜」是兩個對比。但如果我們是光明之子，我們就不必一直提心吊膽。─ 「儆醒」是心智上的警戒，「謹守」卻是道德上的自製。─ 盼望不是「一廂情願的期望」，而是「篤信不疑的期待」。3. 要肯定神的應許(v.9-11)─ 使我們能坦然面對死亡及末日的因素，主要是因為耶穌基督的救恩。結 論(5:11)我們應該「彼此勸慰、互相建立」。討論問題：(1) 你曾有已信主之親人過世的經歷嗎？你覺得4:13-14這段話，在悲痛中能給你安慰嗎？請分享你的經歷。(2) 你對於「主再來」的應許持何種態度？期盼？恐慌？淡然？謹慎？你覺得主再來的日子近了嗎？請分享你的觀點。(3) 我們要如何在日常生活中保持儆醒與謹守？最後的囑咐帖撒羅尼迦前書 5:12-28莊祖鯤牧師 6/25/2000前 言由於帖撒羅尼迦的信徒才剛信主不久，因此保羅要提醒他們如何過教會的群體生活。在這一段經文中，保羅一連用了五次「弟兄們」(v.12,13,25,26,27)，表示他和他們之間的親密關係。I. 對教會領袖的態度(5:12-13)1. 教牧同工勞苦地從事兩種主要職責(v.12b)A. 治理B. 勸戒2. 信徒們對教牧同工的態度(v.12a,13)A. 敬重B. 用愛心格外尊重C. 彼此和睦II. 對弟兄姊妹的態度(5:14-15)1. 對在信仰上軟弱者─以真誠的愛心相待(v.14)A. 警戒不務正業者(idle)B. 勉勵灰心者C. 扶助靈性軟弱者D. 忍耐眾人2. 對得罪我們的人─追求良善(v.15)A. 不可「以惡報惡」B. 要追求良善III. 對靈性生活的態度(5:16-22)1. 要常常喜樂(v.16)2. 要不住地禱告(v.17)3. 要凡事謝恩(v.18)4. 要分辨並遵行神的話語(v.19-22)IV. 結語：祈求與祝福(5:23-28)1. 為信徒的「成聖」祈求(v.23-24)2. 請信徒為他禱告(v.25)3. 囑咐他們彼此真誠地問安(v.26)4. 祝福(v.28)問題討論：(1) 你覺得我們教會對傳道人及其它配搭同工的態度如何？有沒有需要改進的地方？請分享。(2) 你認為在我們團契或小組中，有沒有做到5:14-15所教導的原則？有那些是我們應該加強的地方？(3) 在你個人對神話語的學習及聽從上，你認為你最大的弱點是甚麼？有甚麼改進的方法嗎？The Nightmare of the End Time1 Thessalonians 4:13-5:11Rev. Tsu-Kung Chuang 6/11/2000IntroductionTwo distinct problems have always fascinated and often perplexed human minds. The first relates to what happens after death. The second relates to what will happen at the end of the world. The first is the problem of bereavement, and concerns others who have died. The second is the problem of judgment, and concerns us as well.I. Be Hopeful(4:13-18)Death and dying were no less problems for ancient than modern people. Death is a fact of life. Death is not an accident; it is an appointment. There is a gravestone in an old British cemetery close to Windsor Castle. It read:Pause, my friend, as you walk by; As you are now, so once was I.As I am now, so you will be.Prepare, my friend, to follow me!If we should die today, where would our soul go?1. The Return(v.14-16)The hardest thing about death is separation from our loved ones. There is ample evidence that among pagans generally there was a sad sense of hopelessness in the face of death. Their mourning was due to their ignorance, only knowledge could inspire true Christian hope. We observe that Paul does not forbid us to grieve altogether. Mourning is natural, even for a while emotionally necessary. It would be very unnatural, indeed unhuman, not to mourn when we lose somebody near and dear to us. What Paul prohibits is not grief but hopeless grief. 2. The Resurrection(v.14-16)From Christian’s perspective, death is only temporary. As sleep is followed by an awakening, so death will be followed by resurrection. However, Paul did not say that the soul went to sleep at death. He made it clear that the soul of the believer went to be with the Lord (v.14). It is not the soul that sleeps; it is the body. However, we are waiting for the redemption of our body too (Rom.8:23).However, the resurrection of unbelievers would be different in character from the resurrection of believers: the resurrection of believers was their participation in Christ’s resurrection.How could our bodies be resurrected, when the elements of the body would decay and become a part of the earth? Paul argued for the resurrection in 1 Corinthians 15:35ff. He pointed out that the resurrection of the human body is like the growing of a plant from a seed. The flower is not the identical seed that was planted, yet there is continuity from seed to plant. Christians shall receive glorified bodies, like the glorified body of Christ (1 Cor. 15:47-58). The dead body is the “seed” that is planted in the ground; the resurrection body is the “flower” that comes from that seed.3. The Rapture(v.17a)The word “rapture” is not used in this section, but that is the literal meaning of “caught up”. The Latin word “rapto” means “to seize, to carry off;” and from it we get our English word “rapture”. The word rapture are full of meaning. They means: (1) to catch away speedily, for there will be no warning; (2) to seize by force, for Satan will seek to hinder our rapture to heaven; (3) to claim for one’s self, just as the Bridegroom claims the bride; (4) to move to a new place; and (5) to rescue from danger, for the church will not go through the Tribulation.One summer a church camp staff staged an elaborate rapture while the camp director was off the grounds. When he returned, everybody was missing, clothing was on the ground as though people had “passed through” it, a motorboat was circling on the lake without pilot or passengers, and everything in the kitchen was functioning without a cock. A carefully timed phone call from town, (“hey, what’s happening? Everybody’s missing over here!”) only added to the effect. The director admitted later that it really shook him for a minute. Just think of what effect this event will have on a lost world!4. The Reunion(v.17b)The goal of redemption is not just to rescue us from judgment, but to relate us to Christ. It will be a glorious and everlasting meeting. Death is the great separator, but Jesus Christ is the great Reconciler.The reunion bring us the hope and the glorious expectation. II. Be Watchful(5:1-10)Jesus Christ both unites and divides. Those who have trusted Him as Savior are united in Christ as God’s children. But Christ is also a divider. Faith in Jesus Christ not only unites us to other believers; it also separates us spiritually from the rest of the world. 1. Don’t Be Ignorant(v.1-3)The Day of the Lord is that time when God will judge the world and punish the nations. At the same time, God will prepare His children for the return of Jesus Christ to the earth to establish His kingdom.The unsaved world lives in false security, like the people before the flood (Gen.6) or the citizens of Sodom and Gomorrah (Gen.18-19). Paul gives two comparisons to Christ’s coming: (1) the thief in the night, telling of the surprise and unpreparedness of those affected by it; (2) the woman giving birth, telling of the suddenness and suffering involved. There is an obvious difference between the two illustrations. For although both are sudden, the thief is unexpected, whereas labor (once pregnancy has begun) is expected. In the first case there will be no warning, and the second no escape.On the other hand, we don’t need to speculate the date of the Day of the Lord. However, in church history there is always some people claimed that they “know” the time and hour of the Rapture. For example, in 1843 a Baptist pastor, Rev. William Miller, claimed Jesus would return on that year. Thousands of his followers sold their properties and gathered at the sea shore of Oregon to wait for Jesus. But Jesus was not show up. Rev. Miller then immediately revised his calculation and announced that the correct date should be October 22, 1844. Once again they were disappointed. This is the “Great Disappointment.” Even Rev. Miller apologized and retreated from the movement, some of his followers refused to leave and formed the Seventh Day Adventure. 2. Be Alert and Self-Controlled(v.4-8)Christians who are looking for Christ to come will stay awake and alert; they will not become drunken like the people of the world. “Wake” and “sleep” here mean respectively “alert” and “careless.” Live expectantly. This does not mean putting on a white sheet and sitting atop a mountain. That is the very attitude God condemned (Acts 1:10-11). But it does mean living in the light of His return, realizing that our works will be judged and that our opportunities for service on earth will end. It means to live “with eternity’s values in view.”Believers who live in the expectation of the Lord’s return will certainly enjoy a better life than Christians who compromise with the world. Since we are “sons of the day” we should not live as those who belong to the darkness. In other words, because “the day” is approaching, it is time to wake up, clean up, and dress up. And when we dress up, we had better put on “the breastplate of faith and love; and for a helmet, the hope of salvation” (5:8). Only the “armor of light” (Rom.13:12) will adequately protect us in these last days before our Lord returns. The sober-minded believer has a calm, sane outlook on life. He is not ignorant, but neither is he frustrated and afraid. He hears the tragic news of the day, yet he does not lose heart. He experiences the difficulties of life, but he does not give up. He knows his future is secure in God’s hands, so he lives each day creatively, calmly, and obediently. Outlook determines outcome; and when your outlook is the uplook, then your outcome is secure.3. Be Assured(v.9-10)On what foundation is our Christian hope built? It is not only based how we should behave (awake, alert, self-controlled, well-armed), or on who we are (children of the day and of the light). It should be based on who God is and on what he has done for us. Therefore the ultimate reason why we should be bold rather than faint-hearted in anticipation of the Parousia lies not in who we are but on who God is. Conclusion(5:11)Paul closed this section with the practical application of the Scripture: encouragement and edification. The fact that we will meet our loved ones again and forever be with the Lord is a source of encouragement. And the fact that we will not endure God’s wrath during the Day of the Lord is another source of encouragement. The first is positive, and the second is negative, and both are comforting. 受苦與得榮帖撒羅尼迦後書 1:1-12莊劉真光師母 5/27/2001前
